operator_io_quirks: All table/column names are backtick-quoted in DDL; generated SQL must double-quote them (no spaces/mixed case here, but keep the rule).
Tiny DB: every table has 15 rows except Vehicles=3; read_schema sampling is trivial, no huge-table path exercised.

DATETIME columns store TEXT like 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' (space separator, no T, no timezone); ts_fuzzer dispatch is 'Date|Number(int elements)' because the first element does not parse as int -> Date fuzzer.
lesson_time is VARCHAR(10) holding bare integers '5','6','3' (hour-of-day), NOT a time string; String fuzzer will emit random letters there.
customer_status_code / payment_method_code / lesson_status_code are VARCHAR holding multi-word enum labels ('Bad Customer','Direct Debit','Cancelled') with distinct=2.
country has distinct=1 ('USA'); state_province_county distinct=11 of 15.
Customer_Payments has composite PK (customer_id, datetime_payment); customer_id is also an FK to Customers -> composite-PK member gets max_l0=30.
Lessons.staff_id is nullable FK (notnull=0) to Staff; Lessons.vehicle_id NOT NULL FK to Vehicles (only 3 parent rows -> heavy FK reuse).
All FKs resolve to existing parents; no dangling FKs, no self-references, no non-unique parents.
amount_outstanding / amount_payment / price are DOUBLE stored as REAL; samples are whole numbers (255.0) but Number fuzzer will emit floats.
phone_number / cell_mobile_phone_number / email_address are free-form text with punctuation and '+', '(', ')', 'x' extensions; String fuzzer charset a-zA-Z 0-9() will not reproduce them.
zip_postcode is text with leading zeros ('00005','08938'); String fuzzer may drop leading zeros.
operator_ts_expectations: Date fuzzer picks template from first parsable element -> '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S' (space form); fresh dates uniform in [min,max] of the 5 sampled originals, so date ranges stay near 2016-2018 for Customers/Lessons and 1991-2015 for date_of_birth.
Number fuzzer on INTEGER PKs: full range [-10^0,10^0]=[-1,1] then +-1/+-2 perturbation -> tiny PKs, collisions likely; sample_fresh_primary_keys drops duplicates so tables shrink.

Number fuzzer on DOUBLE (amount_outstanding, price, amount_payment): scale=0 -> range [-1,1] plus +-0.01/+-0.02 -> values ~0, wildly implausible vs original 199-9443 -> FN risk on range predicates (price > 200, amount_payment > 1000).
String fuzzer on VARCHAR(80) names: random a-zA-Z 0-9() strings of length 0-80, plus contaminate suffix/prefix -> no realistic names; LIKE '%Smith%' style predicates will miss (FN).

String fuzzer on customer_status_code / payment_method_code / lesson_status_code: literal pool from train SQL likely contains 'Good Customer','Bad Customer','Credit Card','Direct Debit','Cancelled','Completed' -> those survive via element path; fresh draws produce garbage -> equality predicates on these codes may FP/FN.

String fuzzer on lesson_time (VARCHAR holding '5'..'9'): int-like elements get str(i+1),str(i-1) added, so '4','6','10' appear; predicates like lesson_time = '5' may still hit but lesson_time > '5' semantics shift.

FK fill: Lessons.vehicle_id drawn from Vehicles.vehicle_id (3 values) with replacement -> many duplicate vehicle_ids; Lessons.staff_id nullable but fill_foreign_keys_consistently draws from Staff (no NULLs unless parent empty) -> NULL-rate 0 preserved by accident.

Customer_Payments composite PK: after Number fuzzer on customer_id (tiny ints) and Date fuzzer on datetime_payment, PK duplicates likely -> sample_fresh_primary_keys drops rows, table may shrink below 15.

Addresses has no FK and is level 0; Staff/Customers depend on it; Lessons depends on Customers, Staff, Vehicles -> table_order levels: [Addresses,Vehicles], [Staff,Customers], [Customer_Payments,Lessons].

No CHECK constraints, no UNIQUE indexes beyond PKs -> drop_unique_duplicates is a no-op; NOT NULL on staff_address_id, customer_address_id, customer_status_code, datetime_payment, payment_method_code, lesson_status_code, vehicle_id, customer_id(Customer_Payments) enforced only at insert -> rows with NULL from empty parent would be skipped.

Known TS misses on this DB: FN from implausible numeric ranges (price/amount) and garbage strings (names, phone, email); FP from missing ties (distinct=15 everywhere means GROUP BY / DISTINCT queries return all rows in original but fewer after PK dedup).
